description: ODC (coverage: DELETE a screen that ALREADY EXISTED): the screen WfCovTaskDetail comes from the chain screen-form -> screen-list and is not created here; this job only touches what it inherited. Deleting a screen means handling THREE consumers, and only two are in the interface: the OnClick of the TaskItem of the list WfCovTasks, the OnClick of the button NewButton and - the one nobody looks for - the module itself, because in ODC the ESpace has a DefaultScreen and the first screen created headless took that role; this third one appears in the refusal with the EMPTY path, which is the ESpace having no path at all. The complete refusal is in tests/jobs-odc-negative/delete-screen-in-use.json. The clean path handles each one in its own way: the navigation of the item is REPOINTED to the new screen WfCovTaskEditor (the Destination set rebuilds the arguments by the contract of the destination, so the argument value is written again), the button's is REMOVED together with the button itself because the link only existed to reach the screen that is leaving, and the DefaultScreen of the module moves to the list. With zero consumers the delete passes without force and takes with it the aggregate, the form and the screen action of the screen; the inherited server action WfCovTask_Save is not left orphan because the new screen starts calling it.

ops._why: (1) BEFORE: three real consumers - the two OnClick of the screen WfCovTasks and the IESpace, with an empty path. These are the paths that the refusal of the delete names

ops.name: WfCovTaskEditor
ops._why: (2) the replacement, with the SAME input contract (TaskId): without it the repointed navigation has nowhere to take the identifier
the new screen also takes over the consumption of the INHERITED server action: without this it would be left with no callers when the old screen leaves

(3a) REPOINT: the inherited navigation of the list item now leads to the new screen. The IListItem is not a direct child of the IList: the List keeps it in its IContent, so the path goes through #IContent
(3b) the argument belongs to the NEW destination: the Destination rebuilds the argument list by the contract of the destination, and the value has to be written again
(4) REMOVE: the New button only existed to open the screen in creation mode; without the screen, the link leaves with the button

(5) the consumer that is on no screen: the ESpace of ODC keeps DefaultScreen and the screen to be deleted still had that role. As long as it is the default screen of the module, the delete refuses with a consumer of empty path; the list takes its place
(6) AFTER: must be at zero - one consumer repointed, one removed, one transferred
(7) without consumers the delete passes without force: brokenConsumers=0, and the screen takes with it the aggregate GetTaskById, the form TaskForm and the screen action Save

ops.name: WfCovTaskDetail
ops._why: (8) empty list: the screen left the module
(9) the inherited server action was not left orphan: whoever calls it now is the screen action of the new screen
(10) the list, which had no consumer at all, now has one: the IESpace, for being the DefaultScreen now
(11) read back: Destination and Arguments of the item point to the new screen
